result: For a finite-dimensional bipartite PPT state rho in ANY local dimensions, min(rank(rho),rank(rho^Gamma))<=4 implies SN(rho)<=2. Consequently any PPT state with SN>=3, including a possible 4x4 target, must satisfy rank(rho)>=5 and rank(rho^Gamma)>=5. This deduction explicitly imports known rank-four PPT classification and the known 3x3 PPT Schmidt bound; it is not claimed novel.
imports: Chen and Djokovic, https://arxiv.org/html/1301.2372v1, Proposition 5 and Theorem 22: bipartite PPT states of rank <=3 are separable; a bipartite PPT entangled state of rank4 is supported on a 3x3 subsystem.
Chen, Yang and Tang, https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.03636, Lemma 3: every 3x3 PPT state has Schmidt number at most2.
proof: If rank(rho)<=3, rho is separable. If rank(rho)=4, either rho is separable or the rank-four theorem puts it on a 3x3 subsystem; in the latter case its PPT property and the 3x3 Schmidt theorem give SN<=2. If instead rank(rho^Gamma)<=4, apply the same rank classification to the PPT state rho^Gamma. If rho^Gamma is separable, transposing its product factors makes rho separable. If rho^Gamma is entangled, it is supported on A_3 tensor B_3; partial transpose sends this support to A_3 tensor conjugate(B_3), so rho is itself a 3x3 PPT state and has SN<=2. This proves the minimum-birank statement without assuming partial transpose preserves Schmidt number.
four_by_four_local_support: For a 4x4 PPT state of SN>=3, neither local support dimension can be <=2, and they cannot both be <=3 by the 3x3 PPT theorem. Thus its local marginal ranks must be one of (3,4),(4,3),(4,4), and both global biranks must be at least5. These are necessary conditions only, not a sufficient test or a solution.
limits: The cited theorems are imported, not re-proved or novelty-cleared. The deduction says nothing about rank>=5 cases, does not certify a 2-block-positive witness, and does not solve the general 4x4 target.
